1: # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 24, 2026
4: 
5: The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
6: scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
8: 
9: **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
10: - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
11:   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
12:   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
13:   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
14: - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
15:   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
16:   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
17:   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).
18: 
19: ## Implemented
20: 
21: - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
22:   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
23:   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
24:   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
25:   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
26: - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
27:   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
28:   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
29:   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
30: - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
31:   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
32:   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
33:   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
34:   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
35:   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
36:   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
37:   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
38: - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
39:   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → `Column`/`Row`, `GRID`+lazy grids → `Grid`,
40:   `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView`, `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
41:   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
42:   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
43:   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
44:   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
45:   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
46:   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
47:   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
48:   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
49:   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
50:   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
51:   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
52:   FILL → `anchors.fill`, `-2` HUG → implicit), color, font size/weight/family,
53:   opacity, visible, z, value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
54:   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
55:   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned
56:   style defaults (value props untouched so a slider/toggle doesn't lose
57:   position on echo).
58: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
59:   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
60:   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
61:   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
62:   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
63: - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
64:   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
65:   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
66:   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
67:   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
68:   `DELETE`.
69: - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
70:   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
71:   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
72: - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
73:   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
74:   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
75:   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
76:   init.
77: - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
78:   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
79:   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
80: - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
81:   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
82:   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
83: - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
84:   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
85:   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
86:   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
87:   a bare program name to Qt.
88: - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
89:   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
90:   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
91:   shared ring).
92: 
93: - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
94:   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
95:   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
96:   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
97:   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
98:   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
99:   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
100:   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
101:   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
102:   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
103:   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
104:   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
105:   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
106: 
107: ## Not implemented / gaps
108: 
109: - Pointer `hover`/`leave` flags (`POINTER_MOVE` hovering/leaving) and
110:   `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` listener bits are not yet reported; BackSpace as native
111:   back (text-focus detection) is deferred.
112: - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
113:   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
114:   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
115: - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` either (the spec table is
116:   aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
117:   can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
118:   vehicle (Phase D).
119: - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
120:   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
121: - `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their
122:   background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
123:   `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
124:   `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.
125: - **FILL in Qt positioners**: `Row`/`Column`/`Grid` reject `anchors.fill` on
126:   their children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a stack defers and is
127:   skipped (the positioner sizes it) — cross-axis stretch would need Qt Quick
128:   Layouts (`RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout`). Qt may print "Cannot specify ...
129:   anchors for items inside Row" notes for DSL FILL/alignment patterns; the UI
130:   renders regardless (this is a fidelity gap, not a crash).
131: - **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
132:   `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring` — the
133:   cross-language nav demo vehicle, since the Rust DSL lacks a
134:   `NavigationContainer`.
135: - Lazy views render eagerly.
136: 
137: ## Verified by
138: 
139: `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; offscreen for the FFI
140: tests) — the delta diff suite, the end-to-end FFI batch
141: (`command_batch_crosses_into_cpp_offscreen`), the **full pipeline**
142: (`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`: DSL → engine → frame → shared decode →
143: delta diff → FFI → live QML `Column`/`Text`/`Button`/`Slider` with spacing/value
144: applied and a delta re-applied), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
145: (`pointer_listeners_attach_mousearea`), the event path
146: (`decode_maps_pointer_and_global_events`, `ring_event_writes_pointer_into_ring_and_wakes`,
147: `scheme_event_reapplies_without_waking`, `text_event_string_is_length_prefixed`,
148: `frame_has_reset_detects_meta_reset`), and Phase-B control coverage
149: (`control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, `picker_builds_model_from_option_children`),
150: and the nav adapter (`nav_slot_promotes_and_pushes_root_page`,
151: `nav_depth_push_and_pop`, `nav_replace_same_depth_new_route`,
152: `nav_custom_chrome_bare_pages`). Full workspace: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.
153: Java JNA demo: `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` (headless `RingEventReaderTest`
154: runs in the Maven reactor; the live host mounts `SplitNavDemo`).
155: Demo: `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh`.

(End of file - total 155 lines)
</content>

  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.

  aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
  can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle (Phase D).

  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).

  background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
  `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
  `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.

353:         return;

355:     // Fill the slot's parent when it is a plain container (a positioner like
356:     // Row/Column rejects anchors on its children and sizes them itself).
357:     if (old->parentItem() && !isPositioner(old->parentItem())) {
358:         QObject *anchors = container->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
359:         if (anchors) {
360:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(old->parentItem()));
361:         }
362:     }
363:     g.widgets[slotId] = container;
364:     g.nav_slots.insert(slotId);
365:     g.nav_stacks[slotId] = container;
366:     old->deleteLater();
367: }

388: // Place a destination subtree root into a container, filling it.
389: void placeDestination(QQuickItem *dest, QQuickItem *container) {
390:     if (!dest || !container) {
391:         return;
392:     }
393:     g.pending_fill.erase(dest);
394:     dest->setParentItem(container);
395:     QObject *anchors = dest->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
396:     if (anchors) {
397:         anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(container));
398:     }
399: }

401: // Reconcile a nav slot's page stack against the app's current destination
402: // (single child) + ROUTE + NAV_DEPTH, mirroring the GTK renderer's depth logic:
403: // pop down to depth, then Refresh (same route) / Push (deeper) / Replace
404: // (same depth, new route). The back-stack stays app-owned; this stack is the
405: // renderer's rendered-output cache. Only the top page is visible.
406: void reconcileNav(uint32_t slotId) {
407:     auto sit = g.nav_stacks.find(slotId);
408:     if (sit == g.nav_stacks.end()) {
409:         return;
410:     }
411:     QQuickItem *container = sit->second;
412:     auto rit = g.nav_route.find(slotId);
413:     const QString route = rit != g.nav_route.end() ? rit->second : QString();
414:     const uint32_t depth = std::max(g.nav_depth[slotId], 1u);
415:     const bool custom = g.nav_custom_chrome.count(slotId) > 0;
416: 
417:     // The destination subtree root: the slot's single child.
418:     QQuickItem *dest = nullptr;
419:     for (uint32_t childId : g.children_of[slotId]) {
420:         dest = findWidget(childId);
421:         if (dest) {
422:             break;
423:         }
424:     }
425: 
426:     auto &pages = g.nav_pages[slotId];
427:     auto &tags = g.nav_page_tags[slotId];
428: 
429:     // Pop down to the app's depth (renderer-driven; no NAVIGATE emitted).
430:     while (pages.size() > depth) {
431:         QQuickItem *page = pages.back();
432:         pages.pop_back();
433:         tags.pop_back();
434:         if (custom) {
435:             // The page IS the destination widget (app-owned); just detach it.
436:             page->setParentItem(nullptr);
437:             page->setVisible(false);
438:         } else {
439:             // Detach any destination the wrapper owns so the app-owned widget
440:             // survives the wrapper's destruction.
441:             if (QQuickItem *c = page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content")) {
442:                 const auto kids = c->childItems();
443:                 for (QQuickItem *kid : kids) {
444:                     kid->setParentItem(nullptr);
445:                 }
446:             }
447:             page->setParentItem(nullptr);
448:             page->deleteLater();
449:         }
450:     }
451: 
452:     auto showTop = [&]() {
453:         for (size_t i = 0; i < pages.size(); ++i) {
454:             pages[i]->setVisible(i + 1 == pages.size());
455:         }
456:     };
457: 
458:     if (pages.empty()) {
459:         if (custom && !dest) {
460:             return; // nothing to show yet (reconcile re-fires on the child)
461:         }
462:         QQuickItem *page = custom ? dest : navPageWrapper(/*isRoot=*/true);
463:         if (custom) {
464:             placeDestination(dest, container);
465:         } else if (dest) {
466:             placeDestination(dest, page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
467:             page->setParentItem(container);
468:         } else {
469:             page->setParentItem(container);
470:         }
471:         page->setVisible(true);
472:         pages.push_back(page);
473:         tags.push_back(route);
474:         return;
475:     }
476: 
477:     QQuickItem *top = pages.back();
478:     const QString topTag = tags.back();
479:     if (topTag == route) {
480:         // Refresh in place (signal update / re-emit after a user back).
481:         if (!custom && dest) {
482:             placeDestination(dest, top->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
483:         }
484:     } else if (pages.size() < depth) {
485:         // Deeper -> push a new page.
486:         if (custom && !dest) {
487:             return;
488:         }
489:         QQuickItem *page = custom ? dest : navPageWrapper(/*isRoot=*/false);
490:         if (custom) {
491:             placeDestination(dest, container);
492:         } else if (dest) {
493:             placeDestination(dest, page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
494:             page->setParentItem(container);
495:         } else {
496:             page->setParentItem(container);
497:         }
498:         if (top != page) {
499:             top->setVisible(false);
500:         }
501:         page->setVisible(true);
502:         pages.push_back(page);
503:         tags.push_back(route);
504:     } else {
505:         // Same depth, new route -> replace the top page's content.
506:         if (custom) {
507:             if (dest && dest != top) {
508:                 top->setParentItem(nullptr);
509:                 placeDestination(dest, container);
510:                 dest->setVisible(true);
511:                 pages.back() = dest;
512:             }
513:         } else if (dest) {
514:             placeDestination(dest, top->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
515:         }
516:         tags.back() = route;
517:     }
518:     showTop();
519: }

523:     auto it = g.mouse_areas.find(id);

531: // Attach a MouseArea overlay for a node's EVENT_LISTENERS pointer mask. Only
532: // the requested handler kinds are wired (each already gated by the mask), so
533: // the Bridge's pointer path needs no extra gating.
534: void attachPointerArea(uint32_t id, uint32_t mask) {
535:     detachPointerArea(id);
536:     const uint32_t bits = mask & (1 | 2 | 4); // POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_MOVE | POINTER_UP
537:     if (bits == 0) {
538:         return;
539:     }
540:     QQuickItem *item = findWidget(id);
541:     if (!item) {
542:         return;
543:     }
544:     QString handlers;
545:     if (mask & 1) { // POINTER_DOWN -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_DOWN = 4
546:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onPressed: bridge.pointer(%1, 4, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
547:     }
548:     if (mask & 2) { // POINTER_MOVE -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_MOVE = 5
549:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onPositionChanged: bridge.pointer(%1, 5, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
550:     }
551:     if (mask & 4) { // POINTER_UP -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_UP = 1
552:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onReleased: bridge.pointer(%1, 1, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
553:     }
554:     const QString qml =
555:         QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nMouseArea { anchors.fill: parent;\n%1}").arg(handlers);
556:     QQuickItem *area = createComponent(g.engine, item, qml.toUtf8());
557:     if (area) {
558:         g.mouse_areas[id] = area;
559:         g.listener_masks[id] = mask;
560:     }
561: }

563: // Pathland cross-axis alignment (0=Start,1=Center,2=End,else Fill) -> Qt's
564: // Row/Column `align` (Qt 6.7+, horizontal flags for a Column).
565: int alignFor(uint32_t raw) {
566:     const float f = f32(raw);
567:     const int idx = (std::isfinite(f) && std::floor(f) == f && f >= 0.0f && f <= 3.0f)
568:                         ? static_cast<int>(f)
569:                         : static_cast<int>(raw & 0xFF);
570:     switch (idx) {
571:     case 0:
572:         return Qt::AlignLeft; // Start
573:     case 1:
574:         return Qt::AlignHCenter; // Center
575:     case 2:
576:         return Qt::AlignRight; // End
577:     default:
578:         return Qt::AlignLeft; // Fill -> stretch is the QML default; gap
579:     }
580: }

582: int weightFor(float weight) {
583:     const int w = static_cast<int>(weight + 0.5f);
584:     switch (w) {
585:     case 100:
586:         return int(QFont::Thin);
587:     case 200:
588:         return int(QFont::ExtraLight);
589:     case 300:
590:         return int(QFont::Light);
591:     case 500:
592:         return int(QFont::Medium);
593:     case 600:
594:         return int(QFont::DemiBold);
595:     case 700:
596:         return int(QFont::Bold);
597:     case 800:
598:         return int(QFont::ExtraBold);
599:     case 900:
600:         return int(QFont::Black);
601:     default:
602:         return int(QFont::Normal);
603:     }
604: }

606: // WIDTH/HEIGHT special values: -1 = FILL (anchors.fill parent), -2 = HUG
607: // (implicit size). Positive values set an explicit size.
608: // Apply a pending FILL (anchors.fill) once a widget gains its final parent.
609: // Skipped for positioners (Row/Column/Grid reject anchors on their children).
610: void flushFill(QQuickItem *item, QQuickItem *container) {
611:     auto it = g.pending_fill.find(item);
612:     if (it == g.pending_fill.end()) {
613:         return;
614:     }
615:     if (container && !isPositioner(container)) {
616:         QObject *anchors = item->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
617:         if (anchors) {
618:             if (it->second & 1u) {
619:                 anchors->setProperty("width", QVariant::fromValue(container));
620:             }
621:             if (it->second & 2u) {
622:                 anchors->setProperty("height", QVariant::fromValue(container));
623:             }
624:         }
625:     }
626:     g.pending_fill.erase(it);
627: }

629: void applySize(QQuickItem *item, const char *dimension, float value) {
630:     if (value == -1.0f) {
631:         // FILL: apply once the widget is in its final parent. Props arrive
632:         // before children are inserted, so if the parent is unknown (or a
633:         // positioner that rejects anchors) defer to insert time.
634:         QQuickItem *parent = item->parentItem();
635:         if (parent && !isPositioner(parent)) {
636:             QObject *anchors = item->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
637:             if (anchors) {
638:                 anchors->setProperty(dimension, QVariant::fromValue(parent));
639:             }
640:         } else {
641:             g.pending_fill[item] |= (*dimension == 'w') ? 1u : 2u;
642:         }
643:         return;
644:     }
645:     if (value == -2.0f) {
646:         return; // HUG_CONTENT: implicit size is the default
647:     }
648:     item->setProperty(dimension, static_cast<double>(value));
649: }

675:     case PL_PROP_PADDING_LEFT:

681:     case PL_PROP_HEIGHT:

684:     case PL_PROP_COLOR:

693:     case PL_PROP_OPACITY:
694:         item->setProperty("opacity", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));

696:     case PL_PROP_VISIBLE:
697:         item->setProperty("visible", value != 0);
698:         break;
699:     case PL_PROP_Z_INDEX:
700:         item->setProperty("z", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
701:         break;
702:     case PL_PROP_VALUE:

705:     case PL_PROP_MIN:
706:         item->setProperty("from", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
707:         break;
708:     case PL_PROP_MAX:
709:         item->setProperty("to", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
710:         break;
711:     case PL_PROP_STEP:
712:         item->setProperty("stepSize", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
713:         break;
714:     case PL_PROP_SELECTED:
715:         item->setProperty("checked", value != 0);
716:         break;
717:     case PL_PROP_ENABLED:
718:         item->setProperty("enabled", value != 0);
719:         break;
720:     case PL_PROP_IS_SECURE:
721:         item->setProperty("echoMode", value != 0 ? 2 : 0); // TextField.Password / Normal
722:         break;
723:     case PL_PROP_PROGRESS:
724:         item->setProperty("value", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
725:         break;
726:     case PL_PROP_IS_INDETERMINATE:
727:         item->setProperty("indeterminate", value != 0);
728:         break;
729:     case PL_PROP_SELECTION:
730:         item->setProperty("currentIndex", static_cast<int>(value));
731:         break;
732:     case PL_PROP_NAV_DEPTH:
733:         g.nav_depth[id] = value;
734:         reconcileNav(id);
735:         break;
736:     case PL_PROP_NAV_CHROME:
737:         if (f32(value) >= 0.5f) {
738:             g.nav_custom_chrome.insert(id);
739:         } else {
740:             g.nav_custom_chrome.erase(id);
741:         }
742:         reconcileNav(id);
743:         break;
744:     case PL_PROP_EVENT_LISTENERS:
745:         attachPointerArea(id, value);
746:         break;
747:     case PL_PROP_ACTION_ID:
748:     case PL_PROP_BINDING_ID:
749:         g.gated_ids.insert(id);
750:         break;
751:     default:
752:         break; // unknown/unsupported props are ignored (Qt setProperty is guarded by the switch)
753:     }
754:     Q_UNUSED(value_type);
755: }

808: // Rebuild a PICKER's ComboBox model from its ordered option children's text.
809: void rebuildPickerModel(uint32_t parentId) {
810:     auto cit = g.components.find(parentId);
811:     if (cit == g.components.end() || cit->second != PL_COMP_PICKER) {
812:         return;
813:     }
814:     QQuickItem *picker = findWidget(parentId);
815:     if (!picker) {
816:         return;
817:     }
818:     QStringList model;
819:     for (uint32_t optId : g.children_of[parentId]) {
820:         QQuickItem *opt = findWidget(optId);
821:         model << (opt ? opt->property("text").toString() : QString());
822:     }
823:     picker->setProperty("model", model);
824: }

826: void insertChild(uint32_t parentId, uint32_t childId, uint32_t index) {
827:     QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
828:     if (!child) {
829:         return;
830:     }
831:     g.parents[childId] = parentId;
832:     // Maintain the ordered structural mirror for every parent.
833:     auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
834:     siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
835:     if (index == UINT32_MAX || index >= siblings.size()) {
836:         siblings.push_back(childId);
837:     } else {
838:         siblings.insert(siblings.begin() + index, childId);
839:     }
840: 
841:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
842:         rebuildPickerModel(parentId); // options drive the model, not the visual tree
843:         return;
844:     }
845:     if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
846:         reconcileNav(parentId); // destination subtree swap -> refresh/replace the top page
847:         return; // the destination is placed by the nav adapter, not visually here
848:     }
849: 
850:     QQuickItem *parent = findWidget(parentId);
851:     if (!parent) {
852:         return;
853:     }
854:     child->setParentItem(parent);
855:     flushFill(child, parent);
856:     if (index == UINT32_MAX) {
857:         return; // append (already last)
858:     }
859:     QList<QQuickItem *> siblingsList = parent->childItems();
860:     siblingsList.removeAll(child);
861:     if (static_cast<int>(index) < siblingsList.size()) {
862:         QQuickItem *after = siblingsList.at(static_cast<int>(index));
863:         if (after != child) {
864:             child->stackBefore(after);
865:         }
866:     }
867: }

869: void deleteNode(uint32_t id) {
870:     auto it = g.widgets.find(id);
871:     if (it == g.widgets.end()) {
872:         return;
873:     }
874:     QQuickItem *item = it->second;
875:     g.pending_fill.erase(item);
876:     item->setParentItem(nullptr);
877:     item->deleteLater();
878:     g.widgets.erase(it);
879:     g.components.erase(id);
880:     g.parents.erase(id);
881:     for (auto &kv : g.children_of) {
882:         auto &opts = kv.second;
883:         opts.erase(std::remove(opts.begin(), opts.end(), id), opts.end());
884:     }
885:     g.children_of.erase(id);
886:     g.nav_slots.erase(id);
887:     g.nav_stacks.erase(id);
888:     g.nav_route.erase(id);
889:     g.nav_depth.erase(id);
890:     g.nav_custom_chrome.erase(id);
891:     g.nav_pages.erase(id);
892:     g.nav_page_tags.erase(id);
893:     g.gated_ids.erase(id);
894:     detachPointerArea(id);
895: }

897: // Native back: Escape is a platform back request (global, never node-keyed),
898: // matching the GTK renderer's window-level key controller. BackSpace is
899: // deferred (needs text-focus detection).
900: class KeyFilter : public QObject {
901: public:
902:     using QObject::QObject;
903: protected:
904:     bool eventFilter(QObject *obj, QEvent *ev) override {
905:         if (ev->type() == QEvent::KeyPress) {
906:             auto *ke = static_cast<QKeyEvent *>(ev);
907:             if (ke->key() == Qt::Key_Escape) {
908:                 if (g.bridge) {
909:                     g.bridge->navigateBack();
910:                 }
911:                 return true;
912:             }
913:         }
914:         return QObject::eventFilter(obj, ev);
915:     }
916: };

1: //! The Qt main-loop shell: owns the `Pump` (frames in / events out) and the
2: //! retained renderer, and hands the C++ shell a tick callback so the ring is
3: //! pumped on the Qt main thread between frames — the Qt analogue of the GTK
4: //! renderer's glib idle pump.
5: //!
6: //! Contract (mirrors `pathland-render-gtk`):
7: //! - The renderer **never drains events** — it writes `EVENT` opcodes via
8: //!   `Pump::send_input` and wakes the host; the host drains its own ring.
9: //! - All access is on the Qt main thread; the host re-enters the ring from the
10: //!   wake callback on the same thread (the ring is the decoupling buffer, so a
11: //!   control signal firing during frame apply needs no deferred flush).
12:

27: /// The bidirectional transport surface the renderer pumps: frames in
28: /// (guest → host) and events out (host → guest).
29: pub trait Pump {
30:     /// Read the next guest → host frame.
31:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError>;
32:     /// Write a host → guest raw input as an `EVENT` opcode.
33:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError>;
34: }
35: 
36: impl Pump for RingTransport {
37:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
38:         FrameSource::next_frame(self)
39:     }
40:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
41:         DriverTransport::send_input(self, event)
42:     }
43: }

45: /// A host-supplied event callback, invoked (with no payload) when the renderer
46: /// has written a raw input into the host → guest event ring. The host drains
47: /// the ring itself.
48: pub type EventCallback = extern "C" fn();
49: 
50: /// What to do with a Qt raw input.
51: enum QtAction {
52:     /// Encode + write into the event ring, then wake the host.
53:     Send(Event),
54:     /// A platform color-scheme change: re-resolve tokens in the renderer
55:     /// (no host wake — the re-apply flows back as `SET_PROPERTY` commands).
56:     Scheme(Scheme),
57:     None,
58: }

60: /// Decode a `QtEvent` (C++ → Rust) into an action.
61: fn decode_event(raw: &QtEvent) -> QtAction {
62:     match raw.kind {
63:         ev::POINTER_DOWN => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerDown {
64:             target: raw.node_id,
65:             x: raw.x,
66:             y: raw.y,
67:             secondary: false,
68:         }),
69:         ev::POINTER_MOVE => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerMove {
70:             target: raw.node_id,
71:             x: raw.x,
72:             y: raw.y,
73:             hovering: false,
74:             leaving: false,
75:         }),
76:         ev::POINTER_UP => QtAction::Send(Event::PointerUp {
77:             target: raw.node_id,
78:             x: raw.x,
79:             y: raw.y,
80:             secondary: false,
81:         }),
82:         ev::VALUE_CHANGED => QtAction::Send(Event::ValueChanged {
83:             target: raw.node_id,
84:             value: raw.value,
85:         }),
86:         ev::TEXT_CHANGED => {
87:             // The string is length-prefixed, not guaranteed NUL-terminated.
88:             let slice =
89:                 unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(raw.str_ as *const u8, raw.str_len as usize) };
90:             QtAction::Send(Event::TextChanged {
91:                 target: raw.node_id,
92:                 value: String::from_utf8_lossy(slice).into_owned(),
93:             })

95:         ev::NAVIGATE_BACK => QtAction::Send(Event::Navigate { url: None }),
96:         ev::SCHEME_CHANGED => {

123: fn pump_once(runner: &mut Runner) {

216: // Rust-demo path: a shared `Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>` + a host closure
217: // (mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`). The pump borrow is held across frame
218: // application, so the batch's zero-copy view of the shared ring stays valid.

221: /// Per-run state for the shared-ring convenience path.
222: struct RingRunner {
223:     ring: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>,
224:     renderer: QtRenderer,
225:     on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
226: }

228: // The host's drain-and-respond closure, stored for the wake trampoline
229: // (a regular comment: `thread_local!` doesn't carry doc comments).
230: thread_local! {
231:     static RING_HOST: RefCell<Option<Box<dyn FnMut()>>> = const { RefCell::new(None) };
232: }
233: 
234: fn pump_once_ring(runner: &mut RingRunner) {
235:     let guard = runner.ring.try_borrow_mut();
236:     if let Ok(mut p) = guard {
237:         if let Ok(Some(batch)) = FrameSource::next_frame(&mut *p) {
238:             let frame = batch.frame();
239:             if frame_has_reset(frame) {
240:                 runner.renderer.reset();
241:             } else {
242:                 runner.renderer.apply_frame(frame);
243:             }
244:         }
245:     }
246: }

248: extern "C" fn ring_tick(user: *mut c_void) {
249:     if user.is_null() {
250:         return;
251:     }
252:     // SAFETY: single-threaded (Qt main thread); `RingRunner` outlives `run`.
253:     let runner = unsafe { &mut *(user as *mut RingRunner) };
254:     pump_once_ring(runner);
255: }

257: extern "C" fn ring_host_wake(user: *mut c_void) {
258:     if user.is_null() {
259:         return;
260:     }

262:     let runner = unsafe { &*(user as *const RingRunner) };
263:     if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {

265:     }
266: }

268: extern "C" fn ring_event(ev: *const QtEvent, user: *mut c_void) {
269:     if ev.is_null() || user.is_null() {
270:         return;
271:     }

276:     match decode_event(raw) {

282:             if let Some(cb) = runner.on_event {

284:             }
285:         }
286:         QtAction::Scheme(scheme) => runner.renderer.set_scheme(scheme),
287:         QtAction::None => {}
288:     }

291: /// Run the Qt renderer over a shared `RingTransport`, calling `on_event` (with
292: /// the ring) whenever the renderer wrote raw inputs. Mirrors
293: /// `pathland_render_gtk::run`. Blocks until the window closes.
294: pub fn run<F>(_app_id: &str, title: &str, ring: Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event: F)
295: where
296:     F: FnMut(Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>) + 'static,

301:         let mut cb = on_event;
302:         *h.borrow_mut() = Some(Box::new(move || cb(ring_for_host.clone())));
303:     });
304:     extern "C" fn host_trampoline() {
305:         RING_HOST.with(|h| {
306:             if let Some(cb) = h.borrow_mut().as_mut() {
307:                 cb();
308:             }
309:         });
310:     }
311: 
312:     let mut runner = RingRunner {
313:         ring,
314:         renderer: QtRenderer::new(),
315:         on_event: Some(host_trampoline),
316:     };

1: //! The Qt renderer: shared decode core (`RenderTree`) + a sent-state cache
2: //! that produces the delta command batch handed to the C++ Qt layer.
3: //!
4: //! The engine emits diffs, and this renderer forwards diffs: it keeps a mirror
5: //! of what the C++ layer already has (`sent`) and, per frame, emits only the
6: //! commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero** commands. The C++
7: //! layer stays dumb (applies the batch, resets to renderer defaults on
8: //! `RESET_NODE`).

18: #[derive(Debug, Default)]

30: pub struct QtRenderer {

32:     sent: HashMap<u32, SentNode>,
33:     sent_children: HashMap<u32, Vec<u32>>,

51:     /// The decoded tree (shared renderer core).

66:     /// C++ layer. Unchanged nodes produce no commands.
67:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
68:         self.tree.apply_frame(frame);

70:         crate::ffi::apply(&cmds);

73:     /// Clear the whole scene (`META::RESET`): empty the tree and tell the C++

75:     pub fn reset(&mut self) {

78:         self.sent_children.clear();

82:     /// Compute the delta batch vs the sent-state cache.

85:     /// returned batch is only valid while `self` is not mutated — callers must
86:     /// forward it immediately (as [`Self::apply_frame`] does).
87:     pub fn diff(&mut self) -> Vec<Command> {
88:         let mut cmds = Vec::new();
89: 
90:         // 1. Deletions first: nodes gone from the tree.
91:         let live: HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
92:         let dead: Vec<u32> = self
93:             .sent
94:             .keys()
95:             .copied()
96:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
97:             .collect();
98:         for id in dead {
99:             cmds.push(Command::delete_node(id));
100:             self.sent.remove(&id);
101:             self.sent_children.remove(&id);
102:         }
103: 
104:         // 2. Creates (pre-order, so a parent exists before its children are
105:         //    inserted, and a child before any insert references it).
106:         let order = self.pre_order();
107:         for &id in &order {
108:             if self.sent.contains_key(&id) {
109:                 continue;
110:             }
111:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();

248: fn children_diff(parent: u32, prev: &[u32], next: &[u32]) -> Vec<Command> {
249:     let mut cmds = Vec::new();

1: // Shared C ABI types between the Rust decode core and the C++ Qt widget layer.
2: //
3: // A `PathlandQtCommand` is one delta: Rust produces a batch (mirroring the
4: // opcode engine's "only changes" discipline) and C++ applies it to the Qt Quick
5: // scene. This is deliberately a flat struct — the renderer's FFI boundary stays
6: // a batch of small commands, never a serialized tree.
7: //
8: // Inputs flow back the same way: a `PathlandQtEvent` carries one raw input
9: // (control signal -> C++ -> Rust, which encodes the EVENT opcode and wakes the
10: // host). The renderer never drains events.
11: #ifndef PATHLAND_QT_LAYER_H
12: #define PATHLAND_QT_LAYER_H
13: 
14: #include <stdint.h>
15: #include <stddef.h>
16: 
17: #ifdef __cplusplus
18: extern "C" {
19: #endif
20: 
21: typedef enum PathlandQtCommandKind {
22:     PLQT_CREATE_NODE = 0,   /* a=id, b=componentType(u16 low)                    */
23:     PLQT_DELETE_NODE = 1,   /* a=id                                              */
24:     PLQT_INSERT_CHILD = 2,  /* a=parent, b=child, c=index (u32::MAX = append)    */
25:     PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD = 3,  /* a=parent, b=child                                 */
26:     PLQT_MOVE_CHILD = 4,    /* a=parent, b=child, c=newIndex                     */
27:     PLQT_SET_TEXT = 5,      /* a=id, str=text                                    */
28:     PLQT_SET_PROPERTY = 6,  /* a=id, b=(valueType<<16)|propertyId, c=value       */
29:     PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY = 7, /* a=id, b=propertyId, str=value              */
30:     PLQT_RESET_NODE = 8,    /* a=id — reset renderer-owned style to defaults     */
31:     PLQT_SET_SCHEME = 9,    /* a=scheme (0 light, 1 dark)                        */
32: } PathlandQtCommandKind;
33: 
34: typedef struct PathlandQtCommand {
35:     uint8_t kind;
36:     uint32_t a;
37:     uint32_t b;
38:     uint32_t c;
39:     uint32_t str_len;
40:     const char *str;
41: } PathlandQtCommand;
42: 
43: /* One raw input reported by the Qt layer (C++ -> Rust). */
44: typedef enum PathlandQtEventKind {
45:     PLQT_EV_NONE = 0,
46:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_UP = 1,   /* a control was tapped / pointer released (x,y)   */
47:     PLQT_EV_VALUE_CHANGED = 2, /* a control's semantic value changed (f32)      */
48:     PLQT_EV_TEXT_CHANGED = 3, /* a text field's value changed (str)             */
49:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_DOWN = 4, /* pointer pressed on a listener node (x,y)       */
50:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_MOVE = 5, /* pointer moved on a listener node (x,y)         */
51:     PLQT_EV_NAVIGATE_BACK = 6, /* native back request (Escape), global           */
52:     PLQT_EV_SCHEME_CHANGED = 7, /* platform color scheme changed (value 0/1)     */
53: } PathlandQtEventKind;
54: 
55: typedef struct PathlandQtEvent {
56:     uint8_t kind;
57:     uint32_t node_id;
58:     float x;
59:     float y;
60:     float value;
61:     uint32_t str_len;
62:     const char *str;
63: } PathlandQtEvent;

1: //! Build script for `pathland-render-qt`: locate a Qt6 install via
2: //! `qmake -query`, run moc on the QML-facing bridge, compile the C++ widget
3: //! layer with `cc`, and hand the linker the Qt frameworks/dylibs.
4: //!
5: //! Qt location overrides: `QMAKE` env var (else Homebrew `/opt/homebrew/opt/qtbase/bin/qmake`,
6: //! else `qmake6`/`qmake` on PATH). Linux (CI) ships qmake at `/usr/bin/qmake6` and
7: //! moc at `/usr/lib/qt6/libexec/moc`.
8: 
9: use std::env;
10: use std::path::PathBuf;
11: use std::process::Command;
12: 
13: fn qmake_bin() -> PathBuf {
14:     if let Ok(q) = env::var("QMAKE") {
15:         return PathBuf::from(q);
16:     }
17:     for candidate in [
18:         "/opt/homebrew/opt/qtbase/bin/qmake",
19:         "/opt/homebrew/opt/qt/bin/qmake",
20:         "/usr/local/opt/qt/bin/qmake",
21:     ] {
22:         if PathBuf::from(candidate).exists() {
23:             return PathBuf::from(candidate);
24:         }
25:     }
26:     // Fall back to qmake6/qmake on PATH (Linux CI, other installs).
27:     for name in ["qmake6", "qmake"] {
28:         if Command::new(name).arg("-query").arg("QT_VERSION").output().is_ok() {
29:             return PathBuf::from(name);
30:         }
31:     }
32:     panic!(
33:         "Qt6 not found: set QMAKE=/path/to/qmake (Homebrew: brew install qtbase qtdeclarative, then QMAKE=$(brew --prefix qtbase)/bin/qmake)"
34:     );
35: }
36: 
37: fn qmake_query(qmake: &PathBuf, key: &str) -> String {
38:     let out = Command::new(qmake)
39:         .arg("-query")
40:         .arg(key)
41:         .output()
42:         .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("failed to run {qmake:?} -query {key}: {e}"));
43:     assert!(out.status.success(), "qmake -query {key} failed");
44:     String::from_utf8(out.stdout)
45:         .expect("qmake output not UTF-8")
46:         .trim()
47:         .to_string()
48: }
49: 
50: fn moc_name(header: &str) -> String {
51:     let base = header
52:         .rsplit('/')
53:         .next()
54:         .unwrap_or(header)
55:         .strip_suffix(".h")
56:         .unwrap_or(header);
57:     format!("moc_{base}")
58: }
59: 
60: fn find_moc(qmake: &PathBuf) -> PathBuf {
61:     let qt_bin = qmake.parent().expect("qmake must live in a bin dir");
62:     let prefix = qt_bin.parent().expect("qmake bin has a prefix");
63:     let candidates = [
64:         qt_bin.join("moc"),
65:         qt_bin.join("moc6"),
66:         prefix.join("share/qt/libexec/moc"),
67:         PathBuf::from("/opt/homebrew/share/qt/libexec/moc"),
68:         PathBuf::from("/usr/local/share/qt/libexec/moc"),
69:         PathBuf::from("/usr/lib/qt6/libexec/moc"),
70:         PathBuf::from("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt6/libexec/moc"),
71:     ];
72:     for c in &candidates {
73:         if c.exists() {
74:             return c.clone();
75:         }
76:     }
77:     for name in ["moc", "moc6"] {
78:         if Command::new(name).arg("-V").output().is_ok() {
79:             return PathBuf::from(name);
80:         }
81:     }
82:     panic!(
83:         "moc not found (looked next to qmake and in standard Qt libexec paths); set QMAKE to a qtbase qmake"
84:     );

89:     let headers = qmake_query(&qmake, "QT_INSTALL_HEADERS");

93:     // bridge via context-property invokables, so only Core/Qml/Quick + the

95:     let modules = ["QtCore", "QtGui", "QtQml", "QtQuick"];

97:     let framework_dir = |m: &str| PathBuf::from(&libs).join(format!("{m}.framework"));

107:     let framework_header_dirs = |framework: &str| -> Vec<String> {

1: //! # Pathland Qt Quick desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native Qt Quick app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory
4: //! ring** and the shared **Qt renderer** (`pathland-render-qt`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter
7: //! emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and the Qt renderer
8: //! maps them onto a Qt Quick scene (Row/Column/Text/Button/TextField/Slider).
9: //! The demo never touches Qt APIs directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::listener;
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{
25:     assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Color, Node, Slider, View, ViewExt,
26: };
27: 
28: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.QtDemo";
29: 
30: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
31: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
32: 
33: /// Mark a node as a value-reporting control (`BINDING_ID`), so the renderer
34: /// gates its `VALUE_CHANGED` events back to the app. The Rust DSL does not yet
35: /// expose signal property bindings, so the demo marks the slider directly on
36: /// the retained tree (the protocol's "this node reports" marker).
37: fn mark_value_bound(node: &mut Node) {
38:     if node.component == pathland_view::Component::Slider {
39:         node.properties
40:             .insert(pathland_core::property_id::BINDING_ID, 1);
41:     }
42:     for child in &mut node.children {
43:         mark_value_bound(child);
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter + slider value. This is the
48: /// developer's authoring surface.
49: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>, slider_value: &Rc<RefCell<f32>>) -> Node {
50:     let tap_count = count.clone();
51:     let mut tree = vstack![
52:         hstack![
53:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str()),
54:             button("Increment").on_tap_gesture(move || *tap_count.borrow_mut() += 1),
55:         ]
56:         .spacing(8.0)
57:         .padding(16.0),
58:         text("Pathland · Qt Quick · shared ring").foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_888888)),
59:         // A non-button view (Text) declaring raw pointer listeners — proving any
60:         // element can emit events via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` property.
61:         text("I am a Text with raw pointer listeners")
62:             .pointer_events(listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP)
63:             .foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_0000AA)),
64:         text(format!("Slider: {:.1}", *slider_value.borrow()).as_str()),
65:         Slider {
66:             value: *slider_value.borrow(),
67:             min: 0.0,
68:             max: 10.0,
69:         },
70:         vstack![
71:             text("short"),
72:             text("a much longer label"),
73:             text("x"),
74:         ]
75:         .spacing(4.0)
76:         .padding(16.0),
77:     ]
78:     .spacing(12.0)
79:     .padding(24.0)
80:     .build();
81:     mark_value_bound(&mut tree);
82:     tree
83: }
84: 
85: fn main() {
86:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new()));
87:     let ring = Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new()));
88:     let count = Rc::new(RefCell::new(0u32));
89:     let slider_value = Rc::new(RefCell::new(5.0f32));
90:     let handlers = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TapHandlers::new()));
91: 
92:     // Build + emit the current tree, refreshing the id → tap-callback map.
93:     let emit = {
94:         let engine = engine.clone();
95:         let ring = ring.clone();
96:         let count = count.clone();
97:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
98:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
99:         move || {
100:             let mut tree = build_tree(&count, &slider_value);
101:             assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
102:             let mut h = handlers.borrow_mut();
103:             h.clear();
104:             pathland_view::collect_tap_handlers(&tree, &mut *h);
105:             drop(h);
106: 
107:             let mut ring_ref = ring.borrow_mut();
108:             let mut guest = ring_ref.producer();
109:             guest.begin_frame();
110:             engine.borrow_mut().emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
111:             guest.end_frame();
112:         }
113:     };
114: 
115:     // Initial frame before the renderer starts pumping.
116:     emit();
117: 
118:     // Hand the renderer the shared ring and a wake handler. The renderer writes
119:     // native inputs as EVENT opcodes into the ring and wakes us; we drain the
120:     // ring, run the taps through the recognizer, invoke the matching callback,
121:     // and re-emit. The renderer's idle pump applies the delta.
122:     pathland_qt::run(APP_ID, "Pathland Qt Demo", ring.clone(), {
123:         let emit = emit;
124:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
125:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
126:         let start = Instant::now();
127:         let mut recognizer = pathland_view::TapRecognizer::new();
128:         move |ring| {
129:             let events = ring.borrow_mut().drain_events();
130:             let now_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
131:             let mut changed = false;
132:             for ev in &events {
133:                 // Platform back (Escape/back key) arrives as a global NAVIGATE
134:                 // request with no URL. There is no Rust router yet, so this is
135:                 // surfaced to the console to prove the event reached the app.
136:                 if matches!(ev, pathland_core::Event::Navigate { url: None }) {
137:                     eprintln!("[demo] NAVIGATE back requested");
138:                 }
139:                 // A bound control's value changed (the slider): update the app
140:                 // state and re-emit — the echo-suppressed, VALUE-last renderer
141:                 // path applies it back without a loop.
142:                 if let pathland_core::Event::ValueChanged { value, .. } = ev {
143:                     *slider_value.borrow_mut() = *value;
144:                     changed = true;
145:                 }
146:                 if let Some(target) = recognizer.feed(ev, now_ms) {
147:                     if let Some(handler) = handlers.borrow().get(&target) {
148:                         let mut cb = handler.borrow_mut();
149:                         (&mut *cb)();
150:                         changed = true;
151:                     }
152:                 }
153:             }
154:             if changed {
155:                 emit();
156:             }
157:         }
158:     });
159: }

set -euo pipefail

21:     private static final int CATEGORY_EVENT = 0x03;

23:     /** Ring header: byte offset of the event-arena offset (spec/OPCODE.md, memory.rs). */

27:     private final long ringLen;

29: 
30:     public RingEventReader(Pointer ringPtr, long ringLen) {
31:         this.ringPtr = ringPtr;
32:         this.ringLen = ringLen;
33:         if (ringPtr != null && ringLen >= OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET + 4L) {

37:         }
38:     }

40:     /** Decode consecutive 16-byte opcodes from {@code raw} (a drain buffer). */
41:     public List<Event> decode(byte[] raw) {
42:         List<Event> events = new ArrayList<>();
43:         for (int off = 0; off + OPCODE_SIZE <= raw.length; off += OPCODE_SIZE) {
44:             if ((raw[off] & 0xFF) != CATEGORY_EVENT) {

46:             }
47:             int command = raw[off + 1] & 0xFF;
48:             int flags = u16(raw, off + 2);
49:             int a = i32(raw, off + 4);
50:             int b = i32(raw, off + 8);
51:             int c = i32(raw, off + 12);
52:             Event event = decodeOne(command, flags, a, b, c);
53:             if (event != null) {

56:         }

58:     }

61:         return switch (command) {
62:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN -> Event.pointerDown(a, f32(b), f32(c));
63:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_UP -> Event.pointerUp(a, f32(b), f32(c));

67:             case Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> Event.valueChanged(a, f32(b));

2: //!
3: //! The minimal C ABI for the Pathland SPSC ring buffer + 16-byte opcode engine,
4: //! built as `libpathland_core` (a `cdylib`). Foreign hosts (Java FFM, Swift,
5: //! C#, …) construct the 16-byte opcodes themselves, allocate variable-length
6: //! strings into the bump arena, and push them into the shared ring **in
7: //! place** — the engine stays in Rust, the retained tree / diff stays in the
8: //! host language.
9: //!
10: //! ```c
11: //! void* h = pathland_core_create();
12: //! pathland_core_begin_frame(h);
13: //! uint8_t op[16] = { 0x01, 0x01, 0, 0, 1,0,0,0, 2,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0 };
14: //! pathland_ring_buffer_push(h, op);   // TREE::CREATE_NODE, id 1, vstack
15: //! pathland_core_end_frame(h);
16: //! // read opcodes zero-copy from pathland_core_ring_ptr(h)
17: //! pathland_core_destroy(h);
18: //! ```
19: //!
20: //! Opcode layout (little-endian): `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32]
21: //! [B u32][C u32]` — see `spec/OPCODE.md`.
22:

24: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;

30: struct CoreHost {
31:     ring: RingTransport,

34: fn as_host<'a>(handle: CoreHandle) -> &'a mut CoreHost {

40: /// Read a 16-byte opcode from a foreign pointer.
41: fn opcode_from_ptr(opcode: *const u8) -> Option<Opcode> {
42:     if opcode.is_null() {
43:         return None;
44:     }

46:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(opcode, OPCODE_SIZE) };

53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

1: //! Shared-memory ring transport (zero-copy, SPSC).
2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_core::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_core::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is
7: //! the high-performance local path.
8: 
9: use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout};
10: 
11: use crate::traits::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};
12: 
13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }
25: 
26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Create a ring transport over a caller-provided buffer/layout.
36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /// The memory layout (region geometry).
41:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
42:         &self.layout
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Create a producer view over the shared buffer (writes opcodes + arena).
46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Peak at the raw underlying buffer (for embedding/custom transports).
54:     pub fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
55:         &self.mem
56:     }
57: }

59: impl Default for RingTransport {
60:     fn default() -> Self {

62:     }
63: }

65: impl FrameSource for RingTransport {
66:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
67:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
68:         let mut frames = host.frames();
69:         match frames.pop() {
70:             Some(frame) => Ok(Some(OpcodeBatch::new(
71:                 frame,
72:                 crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
73:             ))),
74:             None => Ok(None),
75:         }
76:     }

82:         // host → guest event ring; the guest drains it via `drain_events`.
83:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);

86:         })

177:     #[test]
178:     fn next_frame_is_zero_copy() {
179:         // The ring is a single shared linear-memory buffer. Reading a frame
180:         // must borrow that buffer in place — never copy the opcode stream.
181:         // Prove two things:
182:         //  1. Reading N opcodes allocates O(1) bookkeeping, not O(N) storage
183:         //     (a copy of the opcode stream would allocate per-opcode).
184:         //  2. The arena string decoded from the frame lives inside the shared
185:         //     buffer (pointer identity), i.e. it is read in place.
186: 
187:         use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout as AllocLayout};
188:         use std::cell::Cell;
189:         use std::thread_local;
190: 
191:         thread_local! {
192:             static COUNT: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };
193:         }
194:         struct Counting;
195:         unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Counting {
196:             unsafe fn alloc(&self, l: AllocLayout) -> *mut u8 {
197:                 COUNT.with(|c| c.set(c.get() + 1));
198:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
199:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.alloc(l) }
200:             }
201:             unsafe fn dealloc(&self, p: *mut u8, l: AllocLayout) {
202:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
203:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.dealloc(p, l) }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         #[global_allocator]
207:         static A: Counting = Counting;
208: 
209:         const OPCODES: usize = 1000;
210: 
211:         let mut ring = RingTransport::new();
212:         let buf_base = ring.buffer().as_ptr() as usize;
213:         let buf_end = buf_base + ring.buffer().len();
214: 
215:         // Producer writes opcodes + a string into the shared buffer (no copies).
216:         let arena_ref = {
217:             let mut guest = ring.producer();
218:             guest.begin_frame();
219:             for i in 0..OPCODES {
220:                 guest.create_node(i as u32 + 1, 0x0001).unwrap();
221:             }
222:             let r = guest.set_text(1, "zero-copy proof").unwrap();
223:             guest.end_frame();
224:             r
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Consumer reads the frame. Count allocations: the opcode stream is
228:         // borrowed, so allocations must be O(1), independent of the opcode count.
229:         COUNT.with(|c| c.set(0));
230:         let batch = ring.next_frame().unwrap().expect("a frame");
231:         let frame = batch.frame();
232: 
233:         let decoded: usize = frame.opcodes().count();
234:         let arena = frame.arena_str(arena_ref).expect("arena string");
235: 
236:         let allocs = COUNT.with(|c| c.get());
237: 
238:         assert_eq!(decoded, OPCODES + 1, "create_node + set_text");
239:         assert_eq!(arena, "zero-copy proof");
240: 
241:         // The arena string is read in place from the shared buffer.
242:         let str_ptr = arena.as_ptr() as usize;
243:         assert!(
244:             str_ptr >= buf_base && str_ptr < buf_end,
245:             "arena string must be borrowed from the shared ring (ptr {str_ptr:#x} outside {buf_base:#x}..{buf_end:#x})"
246:         );
247: 
248:         // No per-opcode copying: a handful of O(1) bookkeeping allocations is
249:         // fine; anything O(opcodes) would mean the opcode stream was copied.
250:         assert!(
251:             allocs < OPCODES,
252:             "reading {OPCODES} opcodes must not copy them (allocations: {allocs})"
253:         );
254:     }

The user is asking a question: "Wait. qt_layer.cpp return handwritten code. Why? Is there no api?"

They're asking why qt_layer.cpp contains hand-written C++ code instead of using a Qt API. Let me answer this question directly and concisely.

The context: The Qt renderer is a hybrid. Rust owns the decode core + delta diff, and C++ owns the Qt application shell and applies the delta command batch to QML items. The C++ layer uses Qt APIs (QGuiApplication, QQuickWindow, QQmlEngine, QQmlComponent, etc.) to create QML items dynamically from QML strings.

The question "is there no api" — Qt Quick DOES have an API, but it's QML-centric. Creating QML items from C++ at runtime is done via QQmlComponent (which is what the code does). The alternative would be writing .qml files and using QQuickView. But the renderer needs to create items dynamically based on the opcode stream, so QQmlComponent with `setData` (compiling a QML snippet at runtime) is the standard way to instantiate QML components from C++.

The code is "hand-written" because:
1. Qt Quick's object model is QML-first; there's no clean C++ API to create a `Column`, `Button`, etc. with arbitrary properties without going through QML. The C++ QQuickItem classes are not meant to be instantiated directly for QML types like Row/Column (they're internal).
2. Each Pathland component type maps to a native QML element (Column, Row, Text, Button...). The renderer builds a small QML snippet per node and instantiates it via QQmlComponent.
3. The delta-diff logic (which commands to apply) is in Rust; the C++ layer is the "dumb" applier. But the property mapping (opcode prop → QML property) requires per-property code because there's no generic "set any property" API — Qt's setProperty handles individual properties, but the mapping from Pathland's numeric property IDs to QML property names (and semantics like FILL→anchors.fill, padding, font) needs hand-written switch logic.

So the answer: Yes, Qt Quick has APIs, and the code DOES use them (QQmlComponent, QQuickWindow, setProperty, etc.). The "hand-written" mapping code is unavoidable because the protocol's numeric property IDs need translation to Qt Quick's declarative model, and QML types (Column, Text, Button) are instantiated through QQmlComponent with QML snippets — that IS the Qt API for dynamic QML creation. There's no higher-level "create a Button with a text" C++ factory in Qt Quick; you either write QML or use QQmlComponent.

The eager FILL anchors referencing the OLD parent (contentItem) after reparenting: Qt warns "Cannot specify anchors for items inside Row/Column". Let me review the crash-hardening. The crash log: SIGSEGV in `pump_once` reading `[runner+8]` (the `Box<dyn Pump>` vtable). Given my changes addressed the FILL stale-anchor issue and the nav-adapter UAF (detaching children before swap), the crash is likely addressed. But let me also consider the `Runner` lifetime issue more concretely.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider the `Runner` crash once more with fresh eyes now that I understand the code better. The `Runner` struct:
```rust
struct Runner {
    pump: Box<dyn Pump>,
    renderer: QtRenderer,
    on_event: Option<EventCallback>,
}
```

It's stored on the stack of `run_with_pump_sized`. The `user` pointer is passed to C++. `qt_tick` dereferences it. For the vtable to be garbage, the stack must be clobbered OR the pointer is stale.

Hmm — actually, I wonder if the crash is a STACK OVERFLOW. The `QtRenderer` is a `RenderTree` with default token tables. When `QtRenderer::new()` runs in `run_with_pump_sized`, it constructs `RenderTree::default()` → `concrete_default_tables()` builds two BTreeMaps with ~30 String-keyed entries. That's on the HEAP (BTreeMap). The struct itself is small.

But wait — the JVM's main thread default stack size... With `-XstartOnFirstThread`, the main thread is the first (AppKit) thread with a LARGE stack. Rust's `run_with_pump_sized` allocates `Runner` there. Qt's event loop + JNA callbacks + Rust apply... if there's deep recursion it could overflow. But the crash is at +0x24 reading a vtable — that's not stack overflow (stack overflow would be at the stack frame setup).

Let me reconsider: could the vtable pointer be garbage because the `Runner` was MOVED? No — `let mut runner = Runner {...}; let user = &mut runner as *mut Runner;` — the pointer is to the stack slot; Rust won't move it (no moves after taking the address... actually taking the address and passing a raw pointer inhibits later moves of `runner`).

Hmm. Actually — you know what, let me reconsider whether the crash could be from the `title` CString. In `run_with_pump_sized`:
```rust
let title = CString::new(title).unwrap_or_else(|_| CString::new("Pathland").unwrap());
unsafe {
    crate::ffi::pathland_qt_layer_run(title.as_ptr(), ...);
}
```
`title` is a local `CString`. Its buffer is heap. `title.as_ptr()` valid during the call. C++ copies it. Fine.

1. Runs (no JVM crash) — `[split] active path: /home` printed (SplitNavDemo mounted, the router works).
2. Renders — but there are QML errors:
   - `QML QQuickImage: Cannot open: file:///.../icons/home.svg` — the icon paths are relative; the QML `Image` source resolves relative to the QML file location (the temp component), not the working dir. The Java DSL sets IMAGE_SOURCE to "icons/home.svg" which resolves relative to the QML component URL. Need to resolve relative to the app's working directory or the file URL.
   - `TypeError: Cannot read property 'implicitWidth' of null` at lines 6-7 of `<Unknown File>` — this is my stack wrapper QML: `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad`. `lay` is null at eval time! Why? Because the `ColumnLayout` inside the wrapper — when the Item's `implicitWidth` binding evaluates, `lay` should be defined (id in the same component). But "Cannot read property 'implicitWidth' of null" means `lay` resolved to null. 

Why would `lay` be null? The `id: lay` is on the ColumnLayout. In QML, ids are scoped to the component. `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth` in the parent Item — `lay` refers to the ColumnLayout child. But if the ColumnLayout component FAILED to instantiate, `lay` would be null! 

Why would ColumnLayout fail? The wrapper QML:
```
import QtQuick 2.15
import QtQuick.Layouts 1.15
Item {
  objectName: "pl1"
  property real plPad: 0
  implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad
  implicitHeight: lay.implicitHeight + 2 * plPad
  ColumnLayout {
    id: lay
    ...
  }
}
```

Hmm — wait, the error is at lines 6-7 (implicitWidth/implicitHeight lines). `lay` null. The ColumnLayout may have failed to create. Why? Possibly because `import QtQuick.Layouts 1.15` — the version. Qt 6 has QtQuick.Layouts version 1.15? The Layouts module versions: 1.0 through 6.x. Version 1.15 might NOT exist! Let me check. Earlier the qmldir showed `QtQuick.Layouts 1.0` ... `2.11` ... `6.7`. Version 1.15 might not be a valid version. If the import fails, the whole component fails → ColumnLayout not created → `lay` null.

Actually, the error says `<Unknown File>:2:1: QML QQuickImage: Cannot open ... icons/home.svg` — line 2 of some component is an Image with source icons/home.svg. That's the Label's Image. And the implicitWidth null errors are from my wrapper.

Wait — if the wrapper's `import QtQuick.Layouts 1.15` were invalid, the component would be a hard error (component isError → createComponent returns nullptr → createNode fails → no widget). But the tests PASSED (renderer_drives_live_qml_scene works with stacks!). So the wrapper QML DID create in the offscreen tests. So `import QtQuick.Layouts 1.15` is valid.

So why is `lay` null in the Java demo but not the tests? Hmm. Actually — wait. In the tests, `widget_child_count(1)` returned 3, meaning the layout exists and has 3 children. So `lay` is NOT null there. 

The difference in the Java demo: the images fail to load (icons/home.svg missing) — the Image component's `onError` or something? No, that wouldn't null `lay`.

Hold on — let me reconsider. `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad` — in QML, when you reference `lay.implicitWidth` and `lay` is a child Item, this creates a dependency. The error "Cannot read property 'implicitWidth' of null" means `lay` evaluated to null at binding creation time. This happens if the ColumnLayout isn't instantiated YET when the binding evaluates — but QML instantiates children before evaluating parent bindings...

Actually — there's a subtle QML ordering: the `implicitWidth` binding on the parent Item is evaluated AFTER the component's object tree is created. `lay` should be valid. UNLESS the ColumnLayout creation failed for THIS specific component.

Wait — actually, let me reconsider: maybe the error comes from a DIFFERENT component. The "TypeError" at line 6-7 of `<Unknown File>`. My wrapper is 11 lines; lines 6-7 are `implicitWidth`/`implicitHeight`. So it IS my wrapper. And `lay` is null → ColumnLayout failed to create in THAT instance.

Why would ColumnLayout fail? Let me think about the NavContainer case: the nav slot is a VSTACK wrapper. When `promoteNavSlot` runs, it does `old->deleteLater()` and creates a nav container. But BEFORE that, the wrapper + ColumnLayout exist. Hmm.

Actually — wait. Let me reconsider the icons error: `QML QQuickImage: Cannot open file:///.../icons/home.svg`. The Image `source: "icons/home.svg"` — relative to the component. My `createComponent` uses `comp.setData(QByteArray(qml), QUrl())` — empty URL. So relative paths resolve relative to the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY? Actually with an empty base URL, QML resolves relative to the application's base URL or cwd. The error shows `file:///Users/.../pathland-qt-demo/icons/home.svg` — so it resolved relative to the CWD (which is `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`). The icons don't exist there. That's a demo data issue (the images are missing), not a renderer bug per se. But the GTK demo presumably loads them from somewhere. Not critical for "renders nothing" — the icons are missing but the labels/text render.

Now the `lay` null issue is the critical one. Let me think harder.

Actually — maybe the issue is the ORDER of QML property evaluation combined with `layoutOf`/child attachment. When `insertChild` attaches a child to the inner layout, the child is a child of `lay`. That's fine.

Hmm, wait — let me reconsider: the error might be from the wrapper's `implicitWidth` binding being evaluated at a time when `lay` (the ColumnLayout) is being REPLACED. In `promoteNavSlot`, I detach the layout (`lay->setParentItem(nullptr); lay->deleteLater();`). After deleteLater, the layout is scheduled for deletion but still exists. The wrapper `old` also deleteLater'd. But `g.widgets[slotId]` is replaced by the container. So the wrapper and its layout are gone. No more binding evals on them. 

Actually — the binding `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth` — when `lay` is deleted (deleteLater → actual deletion at event loop), the binding on `old` (also being deleted) might evaluate during teardown → `lay` null → TypeError. But that's during teardown of the nav slot, harmless-ish (just a QML warning).

Hmm, but the errors appear during initial render. Let me reconsider the SplitNavDemo structure:
- Root HStack wrapper (id 1?) → RowLayout `lay`.
- Sidebar (id 2) wrapper → ColumnLayout.
- ScrollView.
- Nav slot (id N) wrapper → ColumnLayout. On ROUTE → promoteNavSlot → replaces nav slot wrapper with nav container.

So the `lay` null errors could be from the nav slot's wrapper during promotion: when I detach the layout and deleteLater, the wrapper's `implicitWidth` binding references `lay` which is now being deleted → during the deletion, the binding fires → "Cannot read implicitWidth of null".

This is a QML warning, not a crash. But it indicates the wrapper approach has a fragility. More importantly, does it affect RENDERING? Probably not fatally.

But actually — wait, the user's core complaint is "only a sliver of content." The demo now RUNS and prints `[split] active path: /home`. The question is whether the content renders fully now. I can't see the window. Let me think about whether my layout changes actually fix the sliver.

Let me reconsider the geometry:
- Root HStack → wrapper Item anchored to fill the window (via insertChild parentId==0 → anchors.fill contentItem). Good — root fills 1100x720.
- Root's inner RowLayout fills the wrapper (anchors.fill parent). Good — 1100x720.
- Sidebar (200 wide) → child of RowLayout. RowLayout positions it at x=0, width 200 (via Layout.preferredWidth=200 from FrameMod). fillHeight? The root HStack has ALIGNMENT=FILL → applyStackAlignment sets fillHeight on all children of the RowLayout. So Sidebar gets Layout.fillHeight=true → stretches to full height. 
- ScrollView → child of RowLayout. My insertChild sets fillWidth+fillHeight for SCROLLVIEW by default. So ScrollView fills remaining width (1100-200=900) and full height. 
- ScrollView contentItem = its content. The nav slot (VSTACK wrapper) is a child of the ScrollView → attach to ScrollView.contentItem (my fix). The nav slot gets promoted to nav container. The nav container fills... `placeDestination` anchors the dest to fill the container. The container (nav) is a child of ScrollView.contentItem. When promoted, the nav container is created with `old->parentItem()` = ScrollView's contentItem as parent, and anchored fill. Good.
- The nav page (HomeView etc.) fills the nav container → its content renders.

So the layout SHOULD now render the full SplitNavDemo. 

But the `lay` null warnings during nav promotion suggest the wrapper deletion triggers QML binding errors. Let me reduce the noise and avoid the binding-null issue. The root cause: the wrapper's `implicitWidth: lay.implicitWidth` binding holds a reference to the inner layout; when the wrapper is promoted/deleted, the binding errors. 

A cleaner wrapper that avoids referencing the child by id for implicit size: I could skip the implicit size binding entirely and rely on the wrapper being sized by its parent (layouts use the child's implicit size; but the wrapper Item has no implicit size from children → would be 0). That breaks non-filled stacks (Rust demo root would be 0x0 if not anchored... but roots ARE anchored to fill the window now). But inner stacks (Sidebar, SectionCard) with no explicit size would collapse to 0.

Hmm. So the implicit size binding is needed for stacks that hug their content. The `lay` null error only occurs during deletion of the wrapper. Let me guard the binding: `implicitWidth: lay ? lay.implicitWidth + 2 * plPad : 0`. That prevents the TypeError (null check). Let me update the qmlFor to use `lay ? lay.implicitWidth : 0`.

Actually — `lay` in a null-check: `lay ? lay.implicitWidth + 2*plPad : 0`. In QML, referencing `lay` when it might be null is fine with a ternary guard.

Let me update the stack qmlFor to guard against `lay` being null (during teardown).

Also — the icons: the Image source "icons/home.svg" resolves to CWD-relative. The demo runs from `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`, and the icons are presumably in `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/src/main/resources/icons/` or similar. The GTK demo loads them somehow. This is a minor issue — the images fail to load but the demo still renders (text labels). Let me check if the icons exist and whether the Image source should be resolved differently. Actually the error is just missing files — the demo data issue, not the renderer. I'll note it but not block on it.

Let me fix the `lay` null guard in qmlFor. Then rebuild and re-run the Java demo to confirm the warnings are gone and it still works.

Let me update the two stack QML snippets to use guarded bindings.

+**Last updated:** September 28, 2026
 
 The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
 scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
 
 **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
 - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
 - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
 - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
 - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
 - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
-  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → `Column`/`Row`, `GRID`+lazy grids → `Grid`,
-  `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView`, `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
+  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
+  `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
+  padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
+  `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
+  `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`

   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`

 - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
 - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
   `DELETE`.

   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
 - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
   init.
 - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
 - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).

   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
   a bare program name to Qt.

   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
   shared ring).
 
 - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.

input.newString:
- `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their
  background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
  `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
  `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.
- **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
  `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
  defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
  `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly; `Row`/`Column`/`Grid`
  plain-positioner stretch would need `QtQuick.Layouts` everywhere.
